**My reasoning:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, just like my father did. I have about 8 mu. My two sons work in Shijiazhuang now, so it is mostly me and my wife doing the fieldwork. At 67, I cannot manage complicated things or new crops I don't know. I stick to what I know works.

Here it is wheat in winter, corn in summer — that is all I have ever grown, that is what my neighbors grow, and the soil here suits it. I buy my wheat seed from the village supply store — they sell improved varieties the county recommends, better than my old saved seed. For corn I always buy hybrid seed, because the yield difference is obvious to anyone's eyes. I have used Zhengdan 958 for years, I trust it.

I spread compound fertilizer when I plant, then add urea by hand when the wheat is jointing and when the corn is at the big bell stage. I probably use more fertilizer than the extension people say — I worry about a bad harvest more than I worry about cost. I have a well and I pump water when needed. Wheat needs water before winter sets in, then at jointing, then at heading — three times. Corn mostly gets by on summer rain, I'll water once if it looks dry.

My son rented me a rotary tiller for wheat. For corn I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble after harvest — saves my back.
